Blade scraper · guard study for v6 · 2026-10-04

Guard concepts

New outer shapes for the blade guard, made to match the v5 head. The slimmer versions of the wedge are first; the original three concepts follow. Only the outside changes. Inside, every guard keeps the v4/v5 fit: the full-width blade slot, the clearance over the cap and head, the two friction bumps and the lead-in at the mouth.

changed: guard outside unchanged: fit on the cap unchanged: friction bumps unchanged: body, cap, drawer
Update · slimmer wedge

Making the wedge slimmer

The wedge's height comes from what it has to cover: the cap underneath, and the head on top, which is 7.7 mm tall where the guard ends. Thinner walls only buy about a millimetre, so I tried three ways down, from a gentle trim to a different idea.

Slim 1

Slim wedge

The same wedge with 1.2 mm walls instead of 1.6 (three printed lines, still solid) and a thinner, squarer crown over the head. Same length, same fit, same look, just tighter around the parts inside.

Length × height
20 mm; 4.2 mm at the nose, 13.3 at the mouth
Filament
6.0 g
Grip on the cap
12 mm, as now

Good

  • No change in how it fits or prints
  • Thinner nose, so the tip looks finer

Watch

  • Only 1.2 mm lower than the wedge: the head under it is 7.7 mm tall at the mouth, and that sets the height
  • Thinner side walls press the friction bumps a little less firmly
Slim 2

Slim wedge, shorter

The slim wedge ending 3 mm sooner, at x = 15. The head is lower there, so the mouth drops with it. The friction bumps are still inside.

17 mm; 4.2 mm at the nose, 12.1 at the mouth
Filament
5.1 g
Grip on the cap
9 mm

Good

  • A clear step slimmer while still a closed wedge
  • Still covers the whole front of the head

Watch

  • A quarter less overlap with the cap, so a little more play
Slim 3

Open top

The guard only has to cover the exposed 6 mm of blade. So behind the nose its top is cut away over the head: it becomes a slim frame that hooks over the cap side walls, and the sculpted head shows through. The blade edge is still fully enclosed.

Length × height
20 mm; 4.2 mm at the nose, 8.4 at the mouth
Filament
4.6 g
Grip on the cap
12 mm, as now

Good

  • By far the slimmest: 8.4 mm instead of 14.5
  • The head stays visible, so the tool keeps its shape with the guard on
  • Still holds on the cap the same way: the friction bumps on the side walls, and rails over the cap lips

Watch

  • A frame is less stiff than a closed shell; worth a test print to check it does not twist
  • Dirt can get in over the head (not near the blade edge)

All three are checked in the model against the v5 body and blade: no overlaps. The guard can't get narrower than 65 mm, because the 61 mm cutting edge has to pass through its mouth on the way in, so all the slimming happens in height and in the shoulders. Filament is estimated the same way as for the handle (2 walls, 15% infill).

Reference

Current guard (v4)

A box with rounded corners, the full 13.7 mm mouth height from front to back. It does its job, but next to the new head it reads as a separate block.

Concept 1

Wedge

The top runs in one straight line from a thin 5 mm nose up to the mouth, so in profile the guard continues the head's rising line. Over the head it uses the head's own rounded-box section, and the sides fall away in soft shoulders instead of square edges.

Length × height
20 mm; 5 mm at the nose, 14.5 at the mouth
Filament
6.4 g (−1.3 g)
Grip on the cap
12 mm, as now

Good

  • Reads as the tip of the tool, not a box on the end
  • Same fit and same overlap with the cap as the guard you're testing
  • Prints mouth-down like v4, no supports

Watch

  • 0.8 mm taller than v4 at the mouth (the rounded crown needs a little more wall at its corners)
Concept 2

Raked

The wedge with its mouth cut on a slant: shorter underneath, and reaching 3 mm further back over the head on top. From the side the back edge sweeps up the same way the head rises into the grip.

Length × height
17.5 mm underneath, 23 on top; 15.5 at the mouth
Filament
6.6 g (−1.1 g)
Grip on the cap
9.5 to 15 mm

Good

  • The most dynamic side profile
  • Covers more of the head, so it looks most like one piece with the tool

Watch

  • Prints on its slanted mouth: one inside ramp gets steeper than 45° and needs checking in the real build
  • The top back edge comes to a thin point that I'd blunt to about 1 mm
Concept 3

Short sleeve

The wedge cut down to just past the friction bumps. It covers the exposed 6 mm of blade and 6 mm of the cap, and nothing more.

Length × height
14 mm; 5 mm at the nose, 12.2 at the mouth
Filament
4.6 g (−3.1 g)
Grip on the cap

Good

  • Lightest and most compact
  • Smallest thing to lose in a drawer

Watch

  • Half the overlap with the cap, so it can rock more and is easier to knock off
  • Least of the sweep that makes concept 1 match the head
Recommendation

Open top, or the shorter slim wedge

If you want it properly slim, the open top is the only one that changes the proportions: it is 8.4 mm tall instead of 14.5, lets the head show, and keeps the same 12 mm hold on the cap. It deserves a quick test print to check it is stiff enough. If you'd rather keep a closed wedge, the shorter slim wedge is 2.4 mm lower than the wedge for a little less overlap.

Pick one and I'll build it into v6 with drawings, renders and a test print of the guard.
